split.plus_en: Hands public services or functions to private companies or organizations (privatization, vouchers, outsourcing, contract employment)
split.minus_en: Keeps public services and functions in state bodies with directly employed staff
split.statement_en: Public services should be run by state bodies rather than handed to private companies or organizations, even if this costs the budget more.

split.plus_en: Allows or expands paid rides by private drivers through online platforms
split.minus_en: Keeps paid passenger transport limited to licensed taxis and public transport
split.statement_en: Private drivers should be allowed to offer paid rides through apps, even if this cuts the income of licensed taxi drivers.

reason: Most weight is privatization/outsourcing of public services (informal-education vouchers rows 1,3,39; Army Radio privatization rows 2,21,27; bans on contract employment rows 12,16,18,23,28,29,36,37), which the current q53 wording covers, so part 1 keeps it verbatim. About 22% of the weight, however, is the online ride-sharing reform (rows 4,5,6,15,17,35): opening paid passenger transport to private drivers is market competition, not handing a state-run service to private hands, and a voter's view on state-run services does not answer it; it is a distinct, meaningful voter question, so it is split out. Rows 11,14,19 (ambulance funding for women in labor), 13,22 (fare inspectors), 24 (disaster victim identification) and 30 (local-authority share in school budgets) have no clear link to either part and are light.
